skill.name: project-scaffolder
skill.description: Scaffold new software projects with ready-to-use structures, configuration files, scripts, and documentation for common frameworks and languages.
skill.summary: Create consistent project starters for common frameworks, languages, and team workflows.
skill.author: CuriousLearner

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, scaffold placeholders, and framework examples. One medium risk remains because the FastAPI template binds uvicorn to 0.0.0.0, which can expose a development server if reused unchanged. No prompt injection or data-exfiltration intent was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: FastAPI development server binds to all interfaces.
remediation.suggestion: Use 127.0.0.1 as the default host, or clearly document when 0.0.0.0 is required for containers.

remediation.issue: Template examples include placeholder secrets and database URLs.
remediation.suggestion: Keep placeholders in example files and add direct guidance to replace them before deployment.

remediation.issue: Scaffold instructions include many setup commands.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to review generated commands and dependency lists before executing them in trusted workspaces.

content.value_statement: Starting a new project often requires repetitive structure, tooling, and documentation decisions. This skill provides framework-specific scaffolds, configuration examples, and setup guidance for common app types.
actual_capabilities: Generates directory structures for frontend, backend, CLI, library, full stack, and monorepo projects.
Provides setup commands for package managers and development tools.
Creates examples for linting, formatting, testing, CI, and pre-commit configuration.
Includes template files such as README, .gitignore, environment examples, and workflow files.
Suggests framework-specific defaults for React, Express, FastAPI, Go CLI, and monorepo setups.
limitations: Templates require review before production use.
Dependency versions may need updates for current project requirements.
Generated credentials are placeholders and must be replaced.
It does not validate every generated file against your local runtime.

use_cases.title: Create a Frontend Starter
use_cases.description: Build a React or Vue project with folders, testing, linting, formatting, and documentation ready for team review.

use_cases.title: Start an API Service
use_cases.description: Generate an Express or FastAPI service with routing, configuration, tests, environment examples, and basic CI guidance.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Projects
use_cases.description: Create repeatable project layouts that align tooling, documentation, and workflow expectations across multiple teams.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Web App Starter
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a simple frontend project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a React TypeScript starter with Vite, tests, linting, formatting, and a short README for local setup.

prompt_templates.title: API Service Starter
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for a backend service.
prompt_templates.prompt: Scaffold a FastAPI service with routes, configuration, tests, environment examples, and CI guidance for a small team.

prompt_templates.title: Reusable Library Starter
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for a package template.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an npm package starter with TypeScript, build tooling, tests, release notes, documentation, and contributor guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Monorepo Delivery Setup
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for a multi-package workspace.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Turborepo monorepo for a web app and shared packages with CI, workspace scripts, and clear ownership boundaries.

output_examples.input: Create a React TypeScript project with tests and linting.
output: A proposed folder structure for application code, shared components, utilities, tests, and public assets.
Recommended development dependencies for TypeScript, Vite, linting, formatting, and test execution.
Setup notes for local development, quality checks, and the first README draft.

output_examples.input: Set up a FastAPI service for a small product team.
output: A service layout with API routes, core configuration, schemas, database session files, and tests.
Environment example guidance for database, application URL, authentication, and API key placeholders.
CI and development workflow notes for repeatable service setup.

output_examples.input: Create a Go CLI starter with configuration support.
output: A CLI package layout with command files, configuration guidance, Makefile targets, and README sections.
Suggested test, build, clean, and install workflows for a maintainable command-line tool.

best_practices: Review generated commands and dependencies before running them in a trusted workspace.
Replace all placeholder secrets and database values before deployment.
Adapt the generated structure to your team ownership model and release workflow.
anti_patterns: Using scaffolded settings in production without security review.
Keeping placeholder passwords, tokens, or signing keys in real environments.
Adding every suggested tool when the project does not need it.

faq.question: What project types does this skill support?
faq.answer: It covers frontend, backend, mobile, desktop, CLI, library, full stack, and monorepo starters.

faq.question: Can it create complete files?
faq.answer: Yes. It can draft structure, configuration, documentation, and example files for supported stacks.

faq.question: Does it choose dependency versions automatically?
faq.answer: It suggests common dependencies, but you should verify current versions before installation.

faq.question: Is it safe for production projects?
faq.answer: Use it as a starting point. Review security settings, secrets, dependencies, and deployment defaults before production use.

faq.question: Can it help with team standards?
faq.answer: Yes. It can align project layout, documentation, quality checks, and CI conventions across repositories.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The marketplace metadata lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
